channel.title: The Brussels Times
channel.description: Latest Brussels posts from The Brussels Times.

item.title: Brussels celebrates 50 years of metro with an open day and exhibitions
item.description: Across the entire metro network, passengers can enjoy concerts and other artistic performances from 14 to 20 September.

item.title: Three young Belgians charged with membership of a criminal organisation in France
item.description: "The three individuals were born in 2007, so have only just come of age, and are Brussels residents."

item.title: Man armed with Kalashnikov arrested at Brussels-Midi station, investigation launched
item.description: The man had reportedly travelled to Belgium from France and had arrived at the Brussels-Midi station shortly before his arrest.

item.title: Four American climate researchers switch to Brussels university
item.description: "It is not the intention that the researchers sever their ties with their American university."

item.title: What to expect when BRIFF returns to Brussels this Friday
item.description: The ninth annual Brussels International Film Festival begins today, bringing international premieres, Belgian productions and emerging European directors to cinemas across the city.

item.title: Brussels unveils latest school playground to receive 'green' makeover
item.description: A total of 25 Brussels playgrounds will receive a makeover as part of a regional initiative to improve the well-being of children and address climate issues.

item.title: Jobseekers in Brussels are struggling to find roles – here's why
item.description: "Don't expect strong growth on the labour market in the short term," warns a senior economist following a new release of job seeker data for Brussels.

item.title: Brussels rooftop swimming pool is one step closer to reality
item.description: The Brussels Region is moving ahead with plans for a permanent outdoor and indoor swimming complex on the Abattoir site in Anderlecht.

item.title: Two Brussels police officers injured during drug-related arrest in Matonge
item.description: Two police officers were injured after a crowd allegedly tried to obstruct the arrest of a suspected drug trafficker in Brussels' Matonge district.

item.title: New penal code confuses Brussels court in an ongoing major drug trafficking case
item.description: Brussels criminal court heard arguments on how Belgium’s new penal code should apply in an international cocaine trafficking case.

item.title: Brussels' social housing corporation at risk of serious underfunding due to political gridlock
item.description: The organisation risks not receiving €131 million from the Brussels Region this year.

item.title: Brussels Anti-Banditisme specialised brigade seized over €1 million in 2026
item.description: Brigade of the Brussels-West police zone has seized more than €1 million, along with large quantities of drugs and 920,000 counterfeit cigarettes.

item.title: Police vehicle hits cyclist in Woluwe-Saint-Lambert while on call
item.description: A cyclist was hit on Tuesday afternoon by a police vehicle as it was responding to an attempted robbery in Woluwe-Saint-Lambert.

item.title: Two Brussels Metro lines disrupted by burning rails
item.description: The station was evacuated while firefighters put out the smouldering rail sleeper.

item.title: US visitor spending in Belgium jumped 26% this summer
item.description: Belgium is becoming a highly rated destination following celebrity endorsements and travel guide recommendations.

item.title: Heylen Warehouses takes over Audi site in Forest
item.description: Financial details of the transaction have not been disclosed.

item.title: Brussels to build new Dutch-speaking school campus at Tour & Taxis
item.description: The campus will have a primary school and a secondary school, as well as a large sports hall.

item.title: 'I know I'm privileged': A different rentrée for Brussels' international teachers
item.description: A Brussels teacher who moved from public to international education reflects on two very different back-to-school realities.

item.title: Rejected for being ‘too old’ or wearing a headscarf: Discrimination on Brussels’ job market persists
item.description: A candidate can have the right qualifications, the right experience and a strong CV – but never make it to the interview.

item.title: Code yellow warning for drought remains in effect across Brussels
item.description: Authorities are urging people to use mains water sparingly as rainfall in recent weeks has not been enough to restore normal conditions.
